title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction: Problem (E526): transverse vibrations of an elastic rod EF of length a, pinned (simply supported, 'stylo fixa') at both ends E and F, with an additional pin at an interior point L, EL = λa. In modern terms this is the Euler–Bernoulli beam on three simple supports, i.e. a two-span continuous beam. Euler seeks normal modes. He takes the common time factor C sin(ζ + t√(g/k)), which has the same 'simple-pendulum length' k for both spans. With u = s/a and ω = a/f, the spatial factor on EL is y = α e^{uω} + β e^{-uω} + γ sin uω + δ cos uω. On LF the same form holds with primed coefficients. The conditions at L are: deflection zero on each side (I, II); continuity of slope dy/ds (III), since a pin allows rotation but the two portions must make the same angle with the axis; and continuity of curvature d²y/ds², i.e. of the bending moment (IV), since the radius of osculation cannot differ on the two sides. At the pinned ends y = 0 and y'' = 0. These give V (y(0)=0), VI (y''(0)=0), VII (y(1)=0) and VIII (y''(1)=0). The result is eight linear homogeneous equations in eight coefficients. Their compatibility, a vanishing determinant, is the frequency equation for ω. Elimination begins: V and VI give β = -α and δ = 0. Adding VII and VIII gives α'e^ω + β'e^{-ω} = 0; subtracting gives γ' sin ω + δ' cos ω = 0, which continues on the next page. Carried through, the elimination leads to the classical two-span frequency equation, equivalent to coth λω − cot λω + coth(1−λ)ω − cot(1−λ)ω = 0. The page also contains a physical remark from the previous page: a clamped interior point decouples the two spans, whereas a pin couples them.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. Equations I–VIII are correct for y=0 at L on both sides, continuity of y' and y'' at L, and simply supported ends.
The printed equation II has '= δ' cos λω' where '+ δ' cos λω' is meant; this is a typographical slip in print or transcription.

ideas.what: Interface (matching) conditions at an intermediate pin: zero deflection on both sides, continuity of slope and of curvature (bending moment), with a jump in shear allowed
ideas.modern_name: Continuity conditions at an intermediate simple support of a continuous beam
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E526); later systematised for continuous beams by Navier/Clapeyron (statics) and in vibration theory by Rayleigh and others
ideas.where_published: E526, Acta Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 1779 (publ. 1782); discussed in Truesdell's Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11(2))

ideas.what: Piecewise general solution of the beam equation y'''' = y/f^4 with an 8×8 homogeneous system whose determinant gives the eigenfrequencies
ideas.modern_name: Free vibration of a two-span continuous Euler–Bernoulli beam; transfer/assembly of span solutions

ideas.what: Observation that a clamped interior point decouples the two spans, while a pin couples them
ideas.modern_name: Coupling of spans through rotational compatibility

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, correct derivation of the boundary and interface conditions for a pinned two-span beam. The paper and this problem are known and discussed in Truesdell's historical commentary; nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Equation II: '+ γ' sin. λω = δ' cos. λω = 0' should read '+ γ' sin. λω + δ' cos. λω = 0'.
